conversation.content: Start a deployment record for the payments reconciler application.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/service", "value": {"name": "payments-reconciler"}}]
Put it in the staging environment for now.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/environment", "value": {"name": "staging"}}]
Use the usual Kubernetes space for that staging setup.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/environment/namespace", "value": "payrec-stg"}]
Point the public traffic at the staging address we use for this service.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/ingress", "value": {"primaryHost": "payrec.stg.example.internal"}}]
Also include the staging metrics address that matches it.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/ingress/metricsHost", "value": "payrec-metrics.stg.example.internal"}]
Wire it to the staging database credentials.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/secrets", "value": {"database": "payrec-stg-db-credentials"}}]
Use the matching staging token bundle for outbound partner calls.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/secrets/partnerApi", "value": "payrec-stg-partner-token"}]
Send staging incidents to the finance platform on-call group.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/alerts", "value": {"pagerDutyService": "pd-finplat-staging", "slackChannel": "#finplat-staging-alerts"}}]
Keep it on the staging release track.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/release", "value": {"channel": "staging-candidate"}}]
Pin the build to the current reconciler container release from our registry.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/image", "value": {"repository": "registry.example.com/finance/payments-reconciler", "tag": "2.14.7", "pullPolicy": "IfNotPresent"}}]
Run it as two pods and roll updates without taking more than one pod down at a time.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload", "value": {"replicas": 2, "strategy": "RollingUpdate", "maxUnavailable": 1}}]
Give each pod modest resource sizing for steady reconciliation work.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/resources", "value": {"cpuRequest": "250m", "memoryRequest": "512Mi", "cpuLimit": "1"}}]
Cap memory at one gibibyte as well.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/resources/memoryLimit", "value": "1Gi"}]
Have the app listen on 8080 for traffic and 9090 for Prometheus over TCP.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/network", "value": {"httpPort": 8080, "metricsPort": 9090, "protocol": "TCP"}}]
Add the usual health checks so Kubernetes can tell when it is alive and ready.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/healthChecks", "value": {"readinessPath": "/ready", "livenessPath": "/healthz", "initialDelaySeconds": 20}}]
Let those checks time out quickly and run at a normal cadence.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/healthChecks/periodSeconds", "value": 10}, {"op": "add", "path": "/healthChecks/timeoutSeconds", "value": 2}]
Set the reconciliation runtime to use UTC, process 500 records at a time, and actually post adjustments rather than just simulating them.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/runtime", "value": {"timezone": "UTC", "batchSize": 500, "dryRun": false}}]
Run the reconciliation shortly after the nightly payment files land, and avoid overlapping runs.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/schedule", "value": {"cron": "15 2 * * *", "concurrencyPolicy": "Forbid", "successfulHistoryLimit": 3}}]
Keep three failed run records around for troubleshooting.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/schedule/failedHistoryLimit", "value": 3}]
Mark the finance platform team as responsible and route internal questions to their service channel.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/ownership", "value": {"team": "finance-platform", "costCenter": "FIN-042", "contactChannel": "#finplat-service-ops"}}]
Use structured info-level logs and keep trace identifiers in the output.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/logging", "value": {"level": "info", "format": "json", "includeTraceId": true}}]
Scrape Prometheus metrics from the app and keep the standard reconciliation dashboard enabled.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/observability", "value": {"prometheusScrape": true, "metricsPath": "/metrics", "dashboard": "payments-reconciliation-overview"}}]
Run the container with a locked-down security posture.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/security", "value": {"runAsNonRoot": true, "readOnlyRootFilesystem": true, "allowPrivilegeEscalation": false}}]
Add the change ticket and note that Maya Chen approved this rollout today.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/audit", "value": {"changeTicket": "CHG-78421", "approvedBy": "Maya Chen", "approvedDate": "2026-06-08"}}]

conversation_pattern: Center the artifact on a service configured for one environment, where namespace, hostnames, secret references, alert routing, and release channel all follow from the environment's supplied attributes. Around this core, add the realistic, independent details a deployment record would carry that do not depend on the environment, and vary their number from sample to sample. Do not embed a lookup or reference card for any environment inside the artifact; the artifact holds only the current environment's own fields.
edit_pattern: Move the deployment to a different specific environment, and supply the target environment's attributes in master_data.
cascade_pattern: Every environment-governed field takes the replacement environment's supplied attributes: namespace, hostnames, secret references, alert routing, and release channel. Service-specific fields that do not depend on the environment stay unchanged. This is determined because the replacement environment's attributes are provided with the edit.
